1: Out of kindness to me you have spoken of the highest secret, the one said to concern the self. Your words have driven away this delusion of mine.
2: For I have heard from you in detail, you whose eyes are like lotus petals, how beings arise and pass away, and I have also heard of your imperishable greatness.
3: It is just as you have described yourself, highest lord. I wish to see your lordly form, highest of persons.
4: If you think that I am able to see it, lord, then show me your imperishable self, lord of yoga.
5: See my forms, son of Pṛthā, in their hundreds and their thousands, divine, of many kinds, and of many colours and shapes.
6: See the Ādityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the two Aśvins and the Maruts as well. See many wonders never seen before, descendant of Bharata.
7: See today the whole world, all that moves and all that does not, gathered in one place here in my body, Guḍākeśa, and whatever else you wish to see.
8: But you cannot see me with only these eyes of your own. I give you a divine eye. See my lordly yoga.
9: Then, king, having said this, Hari, the great lord of yoga, showed the son of Pṛthā his highest lordly form.
10: It had many mouths and eyes and many wondrous sights, many divine ornaments and many divine weapons raised.
11: It wore divine garlands and garments and was anointed with divine fragrances. It was the god, made of all wonders, endless, with faces on every side.
12: If the light of a thousand suns were to rise in the sky all at once, that would be like the light of that great self.
13: There, in the body of the god of gods, the son of Pāṇḍu then saw the whole world gathered in one place and divided in many ways.
14: Then the winner of wealth, filled with amazement, his hair standing on end, bowed his head to the god, joined his palms and spoke.
15: I see all the gods in your body, god, and also the hosts of the different kinds of beings, Brahmā the lord seated on his lotus seat, all the seers and the divine serpents.
16: I see you with many arms, bellies, mouths and eyes, your form endless on every side. I see no end to you, no middle and no beginning either, lord of all, you whose form is all.
17: I see you crowned, bearing a mace and a discus, a mass of radiance shining on every side. You are hard to look at, bright all around as blazing fire and sun, and beyond measure.
18: You are the undecaying, the highest, the one to be known. You are the highest resting place of all this. You are the imperishable guardian of the everlasting dharma. You are the eternal person: so I believe.
19: I see you without beginning, middle or end, with endless power and endless arms, with the moon and sun for eyes and blazing fire for a mouth, heating this universe with your own radiance.
20: For you alone fill this space between heaven and earth, and all the directions too. At the sight of this wondrous, fierce form of yours the three worlds are shaken, great self.
21: Those hosts of gods are entering you. Some, frightened, praise you with joined palms. The hosts of great seers and perfected ones cry, May it be well, and laud you with abundant hymns.
22: The Rudras and Ādityas, the Vasus and the Sādhyas, the Viśvedevas, the two Aśvins, the Maruts and the drinkers of steam, and the hosts of Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Asuras and perfected ones gaze at you, and all of them are amazed.
23: At the sight of your great form, mighty-armed one, with its many mouths and eyes, its many arms, thighs and feet, its many bellies and its many fearsome tusks, the worlds are shaken, and so am I.
24: For when I see you touching the sky, blazing, many-coloured, your mouths open wide and your wide eyes ablaze, I am shaken to my inner self, and I find neither steadiness nor calm, Viṣṇu.
25: And at the mere sight of your mouths, fearsome with tusks and like the fire of time, I lose all sense of direction and find no shelter. Be gracious, lord of gods, abode of the world.
26: And all those sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra are entering you, together with the hosts of the rulers of the earth, and so are Bhīṣma, Droṇa and that son of the charioteer, together with our own chief warriors too.
27: They hurry into your mouths, which are fearsome with tusks and terrifying. Some can be seen stuck in the gaps between your teeth, their heads crushed.
28: As the many rushing currents of the rivers run only towards the ocean, so those heroes of the world of men enter your mouths, which flame all around.
29: As moths fly at full speed into a blazing fire to their destruction, so too the worlds rush at full speed into your mouths to their destruction.
30: You lick again and again, swallowing all the worlds from every side with your flaming mouths. Your fierce rays fill the whole world with radiance and scorch it, Viṣṇu.
